questions.text: Which of these is the traditional Indian greeting representing respect and harmony?
questions.hint: It is a Sanskrit word meaning "bowing to you".
questions.explanation: Namaste is a respectful form of greeting in Hindu custom, found on the Indian subcontinent.

questions.text: What is the color of the middle band of the Indian National Flag?
questions.hint: It represents peace and truth, and cradles the Ashoka Chakra.
questions.explanation: The Indian National Flag is a horizontal tricolour of saffron at the top, white in the middle, and green at the bottom.

questions.text: In the Ramayana, which bird tried to stop Ravana from kidnapping Sita?
questions.hint: He is characterized as an old, heroic vulture.
questions.explanation: Jatayu was a demigod vulture who fought bravely against Ravana to save Sita but was fatally wounded.

questions.text: Which of these devices is primarily used to input textual data into a computer?
questions.hint: It consists of keys representing letters, numbers, and commands.
questions.explanation: A keyboard is the primary user input device for typing text on computing devices.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an Indian state?
questions.hint: It is a Union Territory containing the national capital.
questions.explanation: Delhi is a Union Territory of India, while Goa, Punjab, and Assam are full-fledged states.

questions.text: Which of the following elements has the chemical symbol "Fe"?
questions.hint: Its Latin name is "Ferrum". It is highly magnetic and found in blood.
questions.explanation: The chemical symbol Fe is derived from "Ferrum", the Latin word for Iron.

questions.text: Who is known as the "Father of the Indian Constitution"?
questions.hint: He was a social reformer, jurist, and India's first Law Minister.
questions.explanation: Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar is recognized as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.

questions.text: Which planet in our solar system has the highest mountain, Olympus Mons?
questions.hint: It is commonly referred to as the Red Planet.
questions.explanation: Olympus Mons is a large shield volcano on the planet Mars, standing at over 21 km high.

questions.text: Which ocean occupies the area between Africa, Asia, Australia, and Antarctica?
questions.hint: It is named after a major South Asian nation.
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean is the third-largest of the world's oceanic divisions, bounded by Asia to the north and Africa to the west.

questions.text: Which country won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup in 2024?
questions.hint: They defeated South Africa in a thrilling final in Barbados.
questions.explanation: India won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup in June 2024 by defeating South Africa under Rohit Sharma's captaincy.

questions.text: In which city did Rabindranath Tagore establish the Visva-Bharati University?
questions.hint: Its name means "Abode of Peace", located in West Bengal's Birbhum district.
questions.explanation: Visva-Bharati was founded by Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore in Santiniketan, West Bengal, in the year 1921.

questions.text: Which of these is the oldest mountain range in India, structurally?
questions.hint: These hills run through Rajasthan and Haryana, heading towards Delhi.
questions.explanation: The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest fold mountain systems in the world, dating back to the Proterozoic era.

questions.text: What was the code name of the Indian Army operation to capture the Siachen Glacier in 1984?
questions.hint: Named after Kalidasa's classical Sanskrit play, referring to a cloud messenger.
questions.explanation: Operation Meghdoot was launched by the Indian Armed Forces in April 1984, securing control over the Siachen Glacier.

questions.text: Which legendary filmmaker wrote and directed the famous "Apu Trilogy"?
questions.hint: He received an honorary Oscar in 1992 and was famed for Pather Panchali.
questions.explanation: Satyajit Ray created the classic Apu Trilogy: Pather Panchali (1955), Aparajito (1956), and Apur Sansar (1959).

questions.text: In the context of standard Indian currency, whose signature appears on the 1 Rupee note?
questions.hint: Unlike other currency bills signed by the RBI Governor, this note is issued directly by the Ministry of Finance.
questions.explanation: Under the Coinage Act, the One-Rupee note is signed by the Finance Secretary of India, while all other banknotes are signed by the Governor of RBI.
